title: Fleet agent contract, version 1
description: The one machine-readable self-description every agent* CLI publishes as `<cli> guide --json`. It carries two layers that used to live in separate, independently authored places: the conceptual contract an agent needs in order to route (guidance, concepts) and the mechanical contract a caller needs in order to invoke (commands with typed arguments). `--agent-help`, `--agent-teaser`, and `--help` are renders of this document, never second authorships of it. This file is normative and is executed directly by scripts/validate-agent-contract.ts — it is not mirrored by it.

schema_version.description: The envelope version the CLI already emits for every other command.

contract_version.description: This document's version, independent of the CLI's own version and of the envelope's schema_version.

guidance.description: Prose routing doctrine: when to reach for this tool, which verb to pick, what a caller habitually gets wrong. Deliberately not structured — AgentSearch's depth routing is judgment, and flattening it into enum descriptions loses it. Rendered verbatim by --agent-help and hoisted into an MCP server's instructions.

global_arguments.description: Arguments every command accepts — --json, --db, --format. Declared once here rather than repeated in each command, which for a 32-command CLI is the difference between a contract and a chore. A consumer building a call surface should normally suppress these: they are transport and storage concerns the caller already fixed, not parameters a model should choose.

commands.description: Every command the CLI dispatches, including the ones no agent should call. Audience decides exposure; omission is never how a command is hidden, because a missing command is indistinguishable from an oversight.

then.description: An agent-facing CLI owes the conceptual layer. An operator CLI owes only meta and commands — a webhook receiver has no routing doctrine, and inventing one is worse than omitting it.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

purpose.description: One or two sentences on what this tool is for. The first thing a router reads.

audience.description: Who the CLI is built for. `agent` requires the conceptual layer and is the only value whose commands are candidates for a generated call surface. `operator` means humans and installers drive it.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

model.description: The domain vocabulary — the nouns and their rules. Free-form per CLI, because a board's items and a vault's documents share no shape.

exit_codes.description: Keyed by the numeric code as a string; the value says what it means.

recovery.description: What a caller should do about it. Present whenever the answer is not obvious from the meaning.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

error_codes.description: Every error.code the CLI can put in an ok:false envelope. Authored here once; the refusal sites in code are the only other place these strings may appear.

read_only_commands.description: Full command paths that never write, space-joined for a nested command — `groom export`, `artifacts list`. Must agree with each command's own `mutates`; the validator checks that.

agent_defaults.description: The ordered opening moves — what to call first, and what to reach for before answering from memory.

name.description: This command's own single word, never a path. `agentwiki artifacts list` is the command `list` inside the command `artifacts`.

audience.description: `agent`: a verb an agent should be able to call, and the default surface a generator exposes. `operator`: real, supported, human-driven — doctor, backup, reindex, serve. `internal`: a protocol handler or subprocess entrypoint that is nonsense to call directly, such as AgentBrowse's `provider`. This field is what answers 'which subcommands form the proper programmatic interface', and it is answered by whoever owns the CLI rather than by the consumer.

mutates.description: Whether a successful call can change durable state anywhere — disk, database, network, or another process. Required for a leaf; meaningless on a group, which is not invocable.

guidance.description: Per-command prose, for the cases where the summary cannot carry the judgment. Optional.

arguments.description: Every argument this exact command accepts, positional and flag alike. Scoped to the leaf that owns it: `--reason` belongs to `artifacts rm`, not to the `artifacts` group, which is what lets a required argument actually be required.

subcommands.description: Present when this command is a group rather than a verb. A group holds its own summary — that is the line `--help` prints for it — and delegates arguments, mutates, and invocation to its leaves.

constraints.description: Relations between this command's arguments that a per-argument type cannot state.

examples.description: Worked invocations. Hand-written help carried these and a contract without them renders help that is visibly worse than what it replaced, which is the one thing adoption may not do.

blocking.description: The command waits on something outside itself and may not return promptly — AgentAttention's `wait`, an `events --follow` stream. A caller with a request timeout needs to know before it calls, not after it hangs.

aliases.description: Other names this exact command answers to, such as AgentBrain's `ingest` for `submit`.

deprecated.description: Present when the command still works but should not be reached for; the value says what to use instead.

then.description: A leaf is invocable and owes the full mechanical description. A group owes only its name, summary, and audience.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

accepts.description: What the command reads from standard input.

required.description: Whether stdin is the only way to supply this input. An agent-audience command should not require it: an out-of-process caller has no pipe, so a command whose only input channel is stdin or a file path is unreachable. AgentAttention's `--context TEXT | --context-file FILE` is the pattern to copy.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

kind.description: `one_of`: at most one may be given, or exactly one when `required` is true. `at_least_one`: at least one must be — AgentBoard's `edit` needs one of --label/--title/--summary, which `one_of` states backwards. `conflicts`: these may not be combined. `requires`: the first argument makes the rest mandatory. A relation conditioned on another argument's VALUE — AgentBoard's `order` anchor, required only when `--to after` — has no kind here and belongs in `description`.

arguments.description: Argument names as spelled in `arguments[].name`, including leading dashes.

required.description: For `one_of`: whether omitting all of them is an error.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.

name.description: Bare name for a positional (`url`), or the long flag with its leading dashes (`--depth`). Short aliases go in `aliases`.

type.description: Deliberately the four JSON Schema scalars, so a consumer can map an argument to a call schema without interpreting anything.

format.description: A refinement of `type`, never a replacement. `ref` is the fleet's tiered slug-or-title-or-phrase resolution. A value grammar inside one argument — AgentSearch's allowlist-xor-denylist `--domains` — has no format and belongs in `description`; the type system does not carry it.

direction.description: For `format: path` only. `out` is a destination the command writes, which an out-of-process caller must be told not to point at an existing file, and which resolves against a working directory it did not choose.

repeatable.description: The flag may be given more than once and accumulates. A flag that instead takes one comma-joined string is not repeatable — say so in `description`, because the two are invoked differently and a caller that guesses wrong silently passes one value.

choices.description: The closed set of accepted values. Present whenever one exists, because it is what lets a consumer build an enum instead of a free string.

default.description: The value used when the argument is absent. Omit when there is none; null is a real default, not an absence.

aliases.description: Short or historical spellings, such as `-j` for `--json`.

csv.description: The flag takes one comma-joined string of values. Composes with `repeatable`: AgentSearch's `--domains` is documented Repeatable AND takes `<a.com,b.com>`, so it is both, and an either/or could not describe it. When set, `format` describes the ELEMENT — AgentBoard's `order --id "a,b,c"` is a csv of refs.

minimum.description: Inclusive lower bound for an integer or number argument, such as AgentBrowse's `--slot` at 0.

maximum.description: Inclusive upper bound, such as AgentSearch's `--limit` at 20.

role.description: What kind of knob this is. A consumer building a call surface should expose only `call`: every global argument across the fleet is output shape, store selection, or meta — things the caller has already fixed, not parameters a model should be asked to choose.

^x_.description: Reserved for a CLI's own extensions. A closed shape plus a frozen contract_version would otherwise make version 2 a fifteen-repository flag day; an x_ key is how one repository experiments without one.
